newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan group leaves for China talks after 22-mth hiatus.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan group leaves for China talks after 22-mth hiatus.

text.p: A Taiwan negotiator whose organisation handles talks with Beijing left for China on Monday, breaking a 22-month hiatus in semi-official discussions between the two rivals.

Lee Ching-ping, deputy secretary-general of the semi-official Straits Exchange Foundation, and his delegation were scheduled to meet mainland officials to discuss problems in a previous agreement on cross-strait document authentication, the state-run Central News Agency said.

Before his departure, Lee said he did not rule out the possibility of meeting senior officials from Beijing's Association for Relations Across the Taiwan Strait, China's counterpart for the Straits Exchange Foundation.

A furious Beijing indefinitely suspended semi-official talks between the Taipei foundation and its China counterpart after Taiwan President Lee Teng-hui made a private, but high-profile visit to the United States in mid-1995.

China, which has viewed Taiwan as a renegade province since the island split from mainland China after a civil war in 1949, said President Lee's visit showed he sought independence for Taiwan rather than reunification with the mainland.
Taiwan still bans all direct official contacts with the mainland, notwithstanding a political thaw in the 1980s that allowed semi-official talks to take place.
Despite Beijing's suspension of the semi-official talks, there have been a stream of private exchanges and visits between the two rivals over the past year.
Taiwan has repeatedly urged China to resume semi-official talks to resolve thorny issues facing both sides -- including fishing disputes, repatriation of airline hijackers and stowaways.
Officials from the Straits Exchange Foundation were not immediately available to comment on the agency report.
The Taiwan delegation would visit Beijing, Zhengzhou, Chengdu and Shanghai. They would return to Taipei on May 7, the agency added.
